notes: A three-rung errand and one of the better-observable quests in the corpus: both of its key items resolve uniquely and they are consumed in sequence, so holding the Vat of martello fuel draws the Martello and holding the Empty fuel vat draws the outfitter again. Bullets 1 and 2 are one act -- you pick the 'Assist with replenishment' menu option and the vat lands in the same breath -- so bullet 2 is step 1's evidence, not a rung of its own. Bullets 3, 4 and 5 are one interaction with one Martello: find it, open its menu, stand where the MENU (not the log) tells you. Splitting them would put two unmarkable rungs in front of the one thing the player can actually be tracked through. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 is a per-Vana'dielian-day cooldown shared with A Mightier Martello across every Abyssea zone, and nothing in the packets reports it. The 'You cannot zone at any point' warning is a real failure mode but not an action. 'Machine Outfitter (Attohwa)' folds to the bare key 'machine outfitter', which exists in every Abyssea zone -- every step carries its zone, so that is disambiguated rather than dangerous. Fame code 'aatt' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

steps.note: near the zone entrance; choose 'Assist with replenishment'. Only one Refuel and Replenish or A Mightier Martello can be completed per Vana'dielian day across all of Abyssea, which the addon cannot see.

the Martellos sit around the Confluxes; any one will do, and it works even at 100% health. Choose 'Prepare to replenish martello', confirm, then face the direction the MENU gives -- the log gives a different and wrong one. Do not zone: that destroys the vat and restarts the quest.
pays Cruor, the amount depending on which Martello was refuelled

The page writes the mob as the plural 'Fallen Evacuees'; the singular is recorded, since mobs are folded and matched live against the mob list. Bullet 4's own body is the step -- unlock the Incinerator Room at (I-7) on map 3 -- while its three sub-bullets are route: the two Banishing Gates on the way, and a Pouch of weighted stones from a ??? at (G-8) on map 1 that lets a solo player through them. That pouch is a real optional detour, but it is a persistent key item a player may already be carrying from any earlier visit, so making it a rung with evidence would let the high-water mark jump forward on something this quest never granted. It stays in the note. The door the Garlaige Key opens is never named on the page, so step 4's target is none rather than an invented door. Bullets 7 and 8 sit under a 'Note:' heading and are a Windurst Mission 8-1 conflict and a suggestion to run Rubbish Day alongside -- neither is a step.

notes:
A courier ladder that returns to Pagnelle three times; the four Pagnelle rungs are separated by real errands, so they are genuinely distinct positions and not a same-NPC merge. The one place this page could have paid off does not: the three rockberries ARE key items, but res/key_items.lua holds them as ids 2201, 2202 and 2203 all named 'rockberry', and the resolver rejects non-unique key-item names by design rather than guessing an id. So step 4 has no evidence at all and the ladder falls back on the session latch across the harvest -- an honest loss, not an oversight, and worth a human's attention because a three-of-three key item is exactly the shape this addon wants. The Sickle IS recorded as a requirement: the page says to bring several because it breaks on nearly every harvest, but a count cannot express 'as many as it takes', so one is recorded and the rest is a note. The six harvesting point locations are alternatives for one act, not six steps, so no grid is committed and they live in the note; they are flagged unordered because any of them will do. Bullet 6 is a proximity cutscene at Rala Waterways (E-11) -- Relentless Storm and Jaroney-Baroney are landmarks the page uses to describe the spot, not entities you interact with, so they are not targets. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing. VERIFY: the 'harvest' group string is removed. A group is an unordered set of STEPS -- "do these in any order" -- and this quest has exactly one harvesting rung, so a group of one asserted nothing and drew nothing extra. The six known harvesting points are alternative locations INSIDE one step, which the step note already carries; the unordered_group flag went with the group.

notes: Three rungs, and the middle one is the whole quest. You do not kill Spinescent Protuberances and you do not collect anything from them -- you stand in front of them until five of their attacks land Amnesia on you. That fits none of the three mob roles cleanly, so 'kill' is used because it is the role that draws the sword glyph on the thing you have to go and engage, and the note says plainly that kills are not what is counted. No count is put on the mob for the same reason: five is the number of amnesia afflictions, not of monsters. Bullet 3 is not a step at all, it is the game telling you the counter has filled, plus a long complaint that the counter is unreliable and advice to strip to a Bullwhip Belt so the effect lands -- an outcome and a tactic, and it is folded into step 2's note. Nothing about the count is in any packet, so step 2 has no evidence and the ladder relies on the session latch to reach the hand-in. The [KI] Restrainment resilience is a header Reward and so proves the quest is over, not that step 3 is done. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing; FLevel is empty.

notes:
Bard AF, and the longest ladder in this batch. 'Level: 50+ Bard' is both gates -- level 50 AND jobs ['BRD'] -- and unlike most AF pages this one really does say 'Repeatable: Yes' and carries Category:Repeatable Quests, so it is taken at its word rather than corrected to false. The header's giver is Imasuke, and Imasuke is where the quest actually enters the log; bullet 1's visit to Mertaire happens BEFORE that, which the page says outright ('Quest wont be listed in log yet'). Mertaire is therefore step 1 and Imasuke stays as start -- and because the runtime treats acceptance as proof step 1 is done, that ordering is exactly right. Both Star ring key items are lost to the resolver, not to the reading: res/key_items.lua holds ids 225 and 226 both named plainly 'star ring', and non-unique key-item names are rejected rather than guessed. So the (tarnished) ring is not recorded as a requirement anywhere and the (indecipherable) ring is not step 4's evidence, and this quest's only observable is the Moon ring (id 227, unique) from Chalvatot. That is a real loss worth flagging. Steps 3 and 4 are two rungs on the same Perennial Snow with a one-Earth-minute wait between them; they are the page's own structure and cost nothing, since consecutive steps on one target are one marker. Bullet 8 is route inside Monastic Cavern and is merged into the travel rung; its sub-bullet about the True Sight Orcish Warlord is a warning. Bullet 10 is two acts, kill then click, and is split. The page writes the object as lowercase 'the altar'; 'Altar' resolves as a real targetable entity, so it carries a marker. VERIFY: demoted to medium, and step 1 (Mertaire) is marked optional. The page says outright that the quest is not in the log until after Imasuke, so Mertaire is a PRECONDITION and by the guide's own rule never a ladder position. The draft's reasoning that the accept-latch makes this ordering right is backwards: core/steps.lua sets best=1 the moment 0x056 reports in_progress, so with Mertaire holding rung 1 the mark lands on rung 2 -- Imasuke, the giver the player has just finished with -- which is precisely the 'talk to me for a quest you just took from me' failure the accept-latch exists to prevent. The real next stop is the Perennial Snow. Marking the rung optional records what it is but cannot move the mark, since the latch sets best=1 whether or not step 1 is optional; only dropping the rung would, and that shifts every step after it, so it is left for a human. Everything from Imasuke onward is read correctly and is unchanged.
